contract.root_option: --root <path> is a global option before subcommand
contract.counts: Lean source occurrences, catalog files and build/license context files are separate
contract.proof_status: unknown-unreplayed for every cached source and operation; mathematical_acceptance=false
contract.source_roles: Existing layout and intake membership; uncataloged current files stay candidate-source-only; all old declared hashes/statuses/verification values and per-binding stale status retained, plus metadata_findings
contract.head_semantics: HEAD frozen and reread during snapshot/CAS; subsequent live byte checks tolerate a containing commit and report changed HEAD separately
contract.expansion: Restores exact GRWTSK source, captured catalogs, toolchain/build/license context, preserving each occurrence even if bytes deduplicate
contract.context_invalidation: Any captured context-file byte change seeds all sources; otherwise exact reverse reachability on old/new import graph union, supporting cycles
contract.failure_policy: Failed attempt receipts/candidate manifests/source blobs remain; no old receipt erased or promoted; no source execution/network acquisition

failures_preserved.observation: Read-only real-repository preflight refused because unrelated shared index has unmerged docs/index.md, docs/mathematics/Logic/index.md, docs/reference/library-summary.json.

remaining_premises: Root integrates and preserves concurrent index conflicts before final actual snapshot. No real snapshot was created by this worker.
Root owns source/documentation/catalog integration and actual pinned Lean proof admission.

Import graph is lexical explicit-import inventory for ordinary module identifiers; unsupported quoted module headers fail closed. Implicit Init imports and external package bytes are outside the graph/snapshot.
Cache-writer lock serializes cooperating writers; immediate complete readback detects observed source/HEAD drift, while sources are not globally locked. No atomic source-freeze theorem is claimed.
Adapter is operational Python, not an extracted or kernel-verified implementation of the separate Lean finite models.
No commits, branches, worktrees or remote changes made.
